analysis:
All three changed files are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. I found no production code change, no new attack surface, and no regression against the threat model.

EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift: the visible head excerpts (lines 1818-2499) are existing tests. They cover:
- Rejection of forged internal schema metadata (originalBooleanSchemaKey) on the local acquire path. The test expects invalidToolPayload, no engine submission, and exactly one release of the reservation (lines 1825-1872).
- Media requests bypassing the bridge text path.
- Cancellation propagation to the engine-minted request id.
- Unloading a bridge and draining its engine.
- Heartbeat KV-backend fallback reason clamping, which limits arbitrary MLX/Metal error text on the wire.
- Prefill deadline and partial-prefill cap config resolution.
These reinforce fail-closed behavior and do not weaken any control. The patch excerpt also adds `.toolCallDelta` event handling and a Qwen3.5 close-only reasoning test. That excerpt is truncated and those added lines are not visible in the supplied numbered text, so I could not inspect them directly. The visible parts of that diff are test plumbing only.

GemmaOpenRouterLiveTests.swift: the live test now assembles streamed tool-call fragments by index, which only affects the test's own assertions. It is gated by live-test environment flags. The empty-string defaults are test-local.

GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift: adds an exhaustive switch case that records an Issue if a `.toolCallDelta` event appears for a named tool_choice. This is a test assertion, not a runtime control.

No T-041 cache-storage or at-rest surface is touched, and no secrets are present. The production implementation of `.toolCallDelta` streaming is outside this batch. Integration should confirm that streamed tool-call deltas are encrypted, sealed or handled the same way as other content chunks (T-008, fail-closed encryption) and that tool_choice constraints remain enforced.
